extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institutions and other recipients of Federal financial assistance (Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and compliance officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards that postsecondary institutions must incorporate into written grievance procedures for complaints of sex-based harassment involving student complainants or respondents, including notice, investigation, evidence access, hearings, determinations, appeals, remedies, and informal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the preponderance of the evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred, unless the recipient uses the clear and convincing evidence standard in all other comparable proceedings, in which case the recipient may elect to use that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both standards require the decisionmaker to evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for its persuasiveness; if the decisionmaker is not persuaded under the applicable standard by the evidence that sex discrimination occurred, whatever the quantity of the evidence is, the decisionmaker must not determine that sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify the parties in writing of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred, including the rationale for such determination and the procedures and permissible bases for appeal, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be simultaneous to parties where required (see §106.46(h)); written determination must include specified elements (description, policies used, evaluation, sanctions/remedies, appeal procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of remedies and sanctions after finding
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a determination that sex discrimination occurred, require the Title IX Coordinator to coordinate provision and implementation of remedies to the complainant and other persons identified as affected, coordinate imposition of disciplinary sanctions on a respondent, notify complainant of sanctions, and take other appropriate prompt and effective steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may not impose discipline on a respondent for sex discrimination prohibited by Title IX unless there is a determination at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures that the respondent engaged in prohibited sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance before imposing disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with §106.45, and if applicable §106.46, before the imposition of any disciplinary sanctions against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must follow all procedural requirements in the cited sections prior to imposing discipline tied to sex discrimination findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disciplining participants for certain conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not discipline a party, witness, or others participating in a recipient's grievance procedures for making a false statement or for engaging in consensual sexual conduct based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects participants from discipline that is based solely on the outcome of the determination itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity in appeals offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer parties an appeal process that, at a minimum, is the same as offered in all other comparable proceedings, including proceedings relating to other discrimination complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For student-involved sex-based harassment complaints at postsecondary institutions, must also offer an appeal on the bases set out in §106.46(i)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal application of additional grievance provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts additional provisions as part of its grievance procedures for handling complaints of sex discrimination, such additional provisions must apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any supplementary rules or processes must not advantage one party over another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may elect to participate in an informal resolution process under §106.44(k) if provided by the recipient, in lieu of resolving a complaint through the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, informal resolution must follow the requirements of §106.44(k) (see also §106.46(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content for sex-based harassment grievance procedures (postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution's written grievance procedures for prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex-based harassment involving student complainants or respondents must include provisions that incorporate the requirements of §106.45 and §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must explicitly adopt the substantive and procedural protections set out in both sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-employee fact-specific inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant or respondent is both a student and an employee, the institution must make a fact‑specific inquiry to determine whether the requirements of this section apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum consider whether the party's primary relationship is to receive an education and whether the alleged harassment occurred while performing employment-related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide written notice to the parties whose identities are known with sufficient time to prepare a response before any initial interview; notice must include information required under §106.45(c)(1)(i)-(iii) and additional specified advisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional advisements must inform parties of presumption of not responsible, right to an advisor of choice (may be attorney), equal opportunity to access relevant evidence or an investigative report, and, if applicable, code of conduct prohibitions on knowingly making false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of additional allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient decides in the course of investigation to investigate additional allegations not included in the original written notice or included in consolidated complaints, it must provide written notice of the additional allegations to parties whose identities are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties are informed of any expansion of allegations during investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of written notice for safety concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If the institution has reasonable concerns for the safety of any person as a result of providing notice, it may reasonably delay providing written notice in order to address the safety concern appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable concerns must be based on individualized safety and risk analysis and not on mere speculation or stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal notice and complainant withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: When dismissing a complaint alleging sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or respondent, the institution must provide the parties simultaneously written notice of the dismissal and the basis for dismissal, except if dismissal occurs before respondent notified then notice only to complainant; obtain complainant's withdrawal in writing if dismissal is based on complainant's voluntary withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency about dismissal bases and documents voluntary withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of meetings and proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, to a party whose participation is invited or expected, written notice of the date, time, location, participants, and purpose of all meetings or proceedings with sufficient time for the party to prepare to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies throughout the investigation and grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal advisor access and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide parties the same opportunities to be accompanied to any meeting or proceeding by the advisor of their choice, who may be an attorney; do not limit the choice or presence of the advisor, though the institution may establish restrictions on the advisor's extent of participation so long as restrictions apply equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors' presence must be equally available; restrictions must be neutral and evenly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to have other persons present
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide parties the same opportunities, if any, to have persons other than the advisor present during any meeting or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parity in presence of support people or witnesses during meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment for expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution has discretion to determine whether parties may present expert witnesses, so long as the determination applies equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows institutions to regulate expert use while maintaining parity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable extensions for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow reasonable extension of timeframes on a case‑by‑case basis for good cause with written notice to the parties that includes the reason for the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures flexibility for legitimate delays while keeping parties informed of reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to evidence or investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide each party and the party's advisor an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible, either by providing access to the evidence or the same written investigative report that accurately summarizes the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an investigative report is provided, the institution must provide access to the relevant evidence upon request; parties must have reasonable opportunity to review and respond prior to determination; for live hearings, review must be provided in advance of the hearing; institution must take reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized disclosure; compliance with this paragraph satisfies §106.45(f)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for questioning parties and witnesses (credibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a process enabling the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility when credibility is in dispute and relevant, before determining whether sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questioning must follow provisions in this subpart and occur prior to a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning process when no live hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If no live hearing, the process must allow the investigator or decisionmaker to ask relevant and not otherwise impermissible questions during individual meetings; allow each party to propose questions to be asked by the investigator/decisionmaker, and provide each party with an audio/audiovisual recording or transcript with enough time to propose follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties can propose and respond to credibility‑challenging questions even without a live hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning process when live hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the institution conducts a live hearing, the process must allow the decisionmaker to ask such questions and either (A) allow each party to propose questions to be asked by the decisionmaker or (B) allow each party's advisor to ask questions, subject to relevance rules; questioning must never be conducted by a party personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advisor‑conducted questioning is permitted and a party lacks an advisor, the institution must provide an advisor of the institution's choice, without charge, for the purpose of questioning; the institution must not appoint a confidential employee as that advisor and may appoint an attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker determination on relevance and exclusion of questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker must determine whether a proposed question is relevant and not otherwise impermissible prior to it being posed, and must explain any decision to exclude a question as not relevant or otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question is relevant and not impermissible it must be asked, except that questions that are unclear or harassing may be excluded after opportunity to clarify or revise; reasonable decorum rules may be applied equally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to respond to questions—weight and inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker may place less or no weight on statements by a party or witness who refuses to respond to relevant and not otherwise impermissible questions, but must not draw an inference about whether sex-based harassment occurred based solely on a refusal to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows consideration of non‑cooperation in credibility but forbids adverse presumptions solely from silence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing logistics and record
rubrics_metrics.description: A live hearing may be conducted with parties together or physically separate using technology enabling simultaneous observation and hearing; the institution must create an audio or audiovisual recording or transcript and make it available to the parties for inspection and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live hearing is optional but, if used, must produce a record and permit party access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of written determination (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination provided simultaneously to parties must include: (i) a description of the alleged sex-based harassment; (ii) information about policies/procedures used to evaluate the allegations; (iii) the decisionmaker's evaluation of relevant evidence and determination whether harassment occurred; (iv) when harassment is found, any disciplinary sanctions and remedies provided and, as appropriate, identification of other students affected; and (v) the institution's procedures for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination regarding responsibility becomes final upon the parties' receipt of the written determination of the result of any appeal, or, if no appeal, when the appeal period has lapsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory appeal bases (postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must offer the parties an appeal from a determination or dismissal on the following bases: (i) procedural irregularity that would change the outcome; (ii) new evidence that would change the outcome and was not reasonably available earlier; and (iii) conflict of interest or bias by the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may offer additional appeal bases so long as they are equally available to all parties; must comply with §106.45(d)(3)(i),(v),(vi) in writing regarding appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution notice and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the institution offers or provides an informal resolution process under §106.44(k) to parties to the grievance procedures under §106.45 and this section, the institution must inform the parties in writing of the offer and their rights and responsibilities and otherwise comply with §106.44(k)(3) in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures written notice and adherence to informal resolution protections and procedures.
